clue.text: There's no charge for this brief spin around midweek

indicators.note: to spin the letters around is to whirl them into a new order

parts.note: the middle of the word week is its two central letters

explanation.surface: A short twirl in the middle of the week comes at no cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' looks like an adjective on 'spin' but is the fodder for 'spin around'; 'midweek' supplies the two central letters of week.
explanation.definitionFit: A giveaway handed out without payment is something there is no charge for.

clue.text: Limp books taken in to flog?

indicators.note: the books are taken inside the other word

parts.note: to flay is to whip or flog
B is an abbreviation for book, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Asking whether books should be bought in to sell, limply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' signals one word placed inside another; B for book is doubled for the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Flabby and limp both describe something soft, slack and lacking firmness.

clue.text: Drink as, for instance, decoration is picked up

parts.note: eg (exempli gratia) means for instance

indicators.note: in a down clue picking up lifts the letters so they read from the bottom

parts.note: gong is British slang for a medal or decoration

explanation.surface: A drink, such as a medal ribbon, is collected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is picked up' turns GONG upwards to GNOG in this down entry. GONG is British slang for a medal.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggnog is a drink of eggs, milk and often spirits, popular at Christmas.

clue.text: Money? A little bit require for a little bit of food

parts.note: bread is slang for money
a crumb is a tiny amount of anything

explanation.surface: Asking whether a small sum is needed to buy a morsel to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A breadcrumb is a tiny fragment of bread, a little bit of food.

clue.text: "The Ashes" piece is likely to be glowing

definitions.text: "The Ashes" piece is likely to be glowing

parts.words: "The Ashes" piece is likely to be glowing
parts.note: read not as cricket's Ashes trophy but as a fragment of a dying fire still hot and red

explanation.surface: A fragment from the Ashes cricket series will probably shine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the England and Australia cricket series; here it is just fireplace ash.
explanation.definitionFit: A coal in the remains of a fire is a small piece of the ashes that still glows.

clue.text: Kind of knot one used

definitions.meaning: a hitch tied with two loops in the bight of a rope, used for hooking loads
a person exploited as a tool by someone else, from the fable of the monkey using a ... to pull chestnuts from the fire

explanation.surface: A knot used by one person.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a sailor's hitch and a dupe made to do another's dirty work.

clue.text: Rapid survey showing our cost OK after certain changes

indicators.note: the letters have been changed around to make a new phrase

explanation.surface: A quick review shows our expenses are acceptable after some adjustments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after certain changes' shuffles OUR COST OK into COOK'S TOUR; the grid's printed OO is a slip for OU.
explanation.definitionFit: A cook's tour, after the travel firm Thomas Cook, is a quick sightseeing trip, hence a rapid survey.

clue.text: DIY? Time, perhaps, to clear up

indicators.note: perhaps hints at another arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Asks whether doing jobs yourself means it is time to clean up.
explanation.definitionFit: To tidy is to clear up, putting things in order.

clue.text: Wraps things up before delivering the goods

definitions.text: Wraps things up before delivering the goods

parts.words: Wraps things up before delivering the goods
parts.note: read as a packer sealing products in advance of sale rather than someone finishing a job

explanation.surface: Someone finishes their work before handing over the goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods packaged before they reach the shop are wrapped in advance, which is exactly this verb.

clue.text: Sage in unknown quantities, say, needing more care when cooked

indicators.note: say marks a word spoken aloud

parts.note: Y is a standard unknown in algebra, so several of them are Ys

indicators.note: cooking the letters mixes them into a new order

explanation.surface: Sage, used in uncertain amounts, needs extra attention when cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns YS into its sound-alike WISE; 'when cooked' shuffles CARE to ACRE. 'Sage' looks like the herb but means a wise person, used ironically.
explanation.definitionFit: A wiseacre is a would-be sage who thinks they know everything; the definition is ironic.

clue.text: Reason university gear is redesigned

indicators.note: redesigning the letters lays them out in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A university's equipment is redesigned for a sound reason.
explanation.definitionFit: To reason with someone is to argue a case logically, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Cold war unlikely to be this

definitions.text: Cold war unlikely to be this

parts.words: Cold war unlikely to be this
parts.note: a cold war is fought without open combat, so it is likely to be free of spilt blood, unlike a hot one

explanation.surface: A remark about the Cold War and its character.
explanation.definitionFit: A conflict with no blood shed is described with this word, as a cold war without fighting would be.

clue.text: Lacking in detail, should speed up the painting

definitions.meaning: a sweeping, general approach that ignores the fine points
a wide paintbrush covers more wall per stroke, so the job goes faster

explanation.surface: Advice that broad strokes will get the decorating done faster.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide paintbrush covers ground fast, and the same phrase describes a general approach that skips fine detail.

clue.text: Jocular girl at a festivity

parts.note: gal is a jokey, informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A cheerful young woman at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive celebration or special entertainment, so festivity is a fair synonym.

clue.text: A sure sign that some letters are missing

definitions.text: A sure sign that some letters are missing

parts.words: A sure sign that some letters are missing
parts.note: read not as undelivered post but as a punctuation mark showing an omission, as in don't

explanation.surface: A hint that some post has gone astray.
explanation.definitionFit: This punctuation mark shows where letters have been dropped in a contraction such as can't.

clue.text: It might be pulled out of the fire in the plant

definitions.text: It might be pulled out of the fire
definitions.meaning: an iron rod heated in the coals until it glows
the kniphofia, a garden flower with spikes of flame-coloured blooms

explanation.surface: Something drawn from the flames among the vegetation.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a glowing fire iron and to the kniphofia, a torch lily with fiery flower spikes.

clue.text: NZ feathers inferior?

parts.note: down is soft fine feathers
under means lower or inferior

explanation.surface: Asking whether New Zealand birds' plumage is second-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Down Under is the informal name for Australia and New Zealand, here abbreviated NZ.

clue.text: Without question, the mischievous child's within the law

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child, and the 's stands for is
licit means lawful

explanation.surface: Without doubt the naughty youngster is acting legally.
explanation.definitionFit: Implicit trust or faith is absolute, held without question.

clue.text: Nothing found in thorough search for fish

indicators.note: nothing is found inside the other word

parts.note: a dragnet is a thorough police search
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing turned up in a wide hunt for fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The dragonet is a small, often brightly coloured sea fish.

clue.text: Highlight the speech I made (said as a warning?)

parts.note: to mark something is to highlight it
the speech I gave consists of my own words

explanation.surface: Someone asks for their speech to be highlighted, perhaps as a warning.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition describes how the phrase is used rather than giving a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is said to warn a listener that a prediction will come true, so it is said as a warning.

clue.text: Pelt with metallic stuff to produce an outburst

parts.note: a pelt is an animal's fur
ore is rock from which metal is extracted

explanation.surface: Throwing metal at someone causes a row.
explanation.definitionFit: A furore is a public outburst of anger or excitement.

clue.text: It's sweet, but not honey, and could be offensive

indicators.note: but not says the honey is removed from the sweet word

parts.note: sweet music is melodious
mel is the Latin for honey

explanation.surface: Something sweet but lacking honey might be unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: MEL is Latin for honey, used in words like mellifluous; 'but not' takes it from MELODIOUS. 'sweet' suggests taste but means tuneful.
explanation.definitionFit: Odious means hateful or repugnant, so something odious is offensive.

clue.text: Sign ball after the record

indicators.note: ball comes after the record, so its letter follows in the answer

parts.note: a log is a written record, like a ship's log
O is round like a ball

explanation.surface: Sign the ball after the record is set.
explanation.definitionFit: A logo is an emblem or sign used by a company or organisation.

clue.text: One tours the Centre with the DJ

definitions.text: One tours the Centre with the DJ

parts.words: One tours the Centre with the DJ
parts.note: read as a sash going round the waist, worn with a dinner jacket rather than a disc jockey

explanation.surface: Someone travels round the town centre with a disc jockey.
explanation.definitionFit: This waist sash wraps the middle of the body and is worn with a dinner jacket.

clue.text: Time right, possibly, for quality

indicators.note: possibly suggests another arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: The right moment may be a matter of quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Merit is worth or excellence, a quality deserving praise.

clue.text: I pioneered, setting up a food shop

indicators.note: in a down clue setting up raises the letters to read from the bottom

parts.note: to pioneer something is to lead it

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of being the first to open a delicatessen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting up' turns I LED upwards to DELI in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A deli, short for delicatessen, is a shop selling prepared foods.

clue.text: The prisoner present is the one to fight

parts.note: con is slang for a convict, a prisoner
to tender something is to present or offer it

explanation.surface: The convict now here is the man to take on.
explanation.definitionFit: A contender is a rival competitor, the one an opponent has to fight.

clue.text: Picture stolen in operation is returned

indicators.note: stolen sits within the other piece, so its letters go inside
returned means the word for operation is read backwards

parts.note: op is short for a surgical or military operation
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: An image stolen during a police operation is handed back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is returned' reads the operation word backwards, and 'in' puts the slang for stolen inside it; 'stolen' looks like the surface verb but is HOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A photo is a picture taken with a camera, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: In a worse condition? Treat it to get improvement

indicators.note: improving the letters reorganises them into a new order

explanation.surface: Something shabby needs treating to make it better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get improvement' shuffles TREAT IT; the irony is that the result means in a worse state.
explanation.definitionFit: Tattier means shabbier or more worn, so it describes something in a worse condition.

clue.text: Hero from Athens, not a name to use indiscriminately

indicators.note: not says the a and the name are dropped from Athens

parts.note: A as written plus N, the usual abbreviation for name

indicators.note: using the letters without discrimination jumbles them up

explanation.surface: Advice that the name of an Athenian hero should not be used carelessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes A and N (name) from ATHENS, leaving THES; 'indiscriminately' then shuffles USE into EUS. 'from Athens' looks like part of the definition but supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Theseus is the legendary Greek hero who slew the Minotaur and became king of Athens.
